slots.label: Heading 1
slots.default: Clinical systems, patient data, and no convenient downtime

slots.label: Paragraph 2
slots.default: Healthcare providers combine special-category personal data with services that cannot simply pause. A clinic whose systems are unavailable is not inconvenienced; it is cancelling appointments and turning patients away, which makes availability a clinical concern rather than an operational one.

slots.label: Heading 2
slots.default: Access control that reflects clinical roles

slots.label: Paragraph 3
slots.default: Who may see a patient record is determined by role and by legitimate relationship, not by convenience. Implementing that properly means role-based permissions, meaningful audit logging and periodic review, so that access can be explained rather than assumed.

slots.label: Heading 3
slots.default: Clinical and practice systems set the constraints

slots.label: Paragraph 4
slots.default: Patient management, imaging and referral systems often have specific requirements for browsers, endpoints and connectivity, and they are rarely flexible. Support work here is mostly about keeping a defined environment stable rather than modernising it for its own sake.

slots.label: Heading 4
slots.default: Recovery time is the number that matters

slots.label: Paragraph 5
slots.default: For a provider running clinics, the meaningful question is not whether a backup exists but how quickly a working system returns. Defining an acceptable recovery time, then testing against it, is the part that turns a backup into continuity.
